AND AWARD DATED 18.04.2015 IN MVC NO.3/2012 PASSED BY THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT AT HUMNABAD.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Challenging judgment and award dated 18.04.2015 passed by Senior Civil Judge and MACT,
Humnabad (for short 'tribunal') in MVC no.3/2012, this appeal is filed.

2. Smt.Preeti Patil Melkundi, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by insurer challenging award of tribunal on ground of failure to provide adequate opportunity to insurer to lead evidence, on finding regarding liability, finding on contributory negligence and on quantum of compensation.
It was submitted that accident in question involved two vehicles, namely a crane bearing registration no.KA-32/B-3458, insured with appellant and a car bearing registration no.KA-39/M-484.
It was submitted that accident occurred on National Highway no.9 and was a head on collision.

Therefore, drivers of both vehicles were required to held equally NC:
2023:KHC-K:6530 responsible.
Non -apportionment of negligence and fastening entire liability upon driver of insured vehicle by tribunal would not be justified.
It was submitted that insured vehicle being a crane would fall under special vehicle category as per Section 10(j) of Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'M.V.Act').
Therefore, driver was required to have licence to drive said category of vehicle.
Since claimant failed to produce such licence, finding against insurer would be untenable.

It was further submitted that insurer had taken a specific contention regarding violation of permit condition by alleging that owner of vehicle (insured) had permitted a person without valid and effective driving licence to drive it and therefore insurer was required to be exonerated under Section 149(2) of M.V.Act.
3.
It was submitted that though accident in question was a personal injury claim, tribunal erred in adding 50% towards future prospects.
It was further submitted that as per Ex.P.6-disability certificate, disability NC: 2023:KHC-K:6530 in respect of limb was 40% and consideration of whole

sentences.text: 4. It was submitted that tribunal did not grant adequate opportunity to appellant/insurer to substantiate its contentions by leading evidence and though applications were filed by seeking for recall of order taking evidence of insurer as 'nil' they were rejected.
Since there was denial of opportunity, he sought for remand of matter back to tribunal.
5. On other hand, Shri B.C.Jaka, learned counsel for claimant sought to justify award.
It was submitted that on 19.02.2015 counsel for insurer submitted no evidence on behalf of insurer.

But,
subsequently applications were filed for reopening of matter for evidence.
Applications were rightly rejected.
Under circumstances, there was no substance in contention of appellant that it was denied opportunity.

6. Insofar as contributory negligence, it was submitted that entire police investigation records NC:
2023:KHC-K:6530 implicated only driver of crane for causing accident due to rash and negligent driving and therefore tribunal was justified in passing award against appellant/insurer.
7.
Insofar as quantum of compensation, it was submitted that accident occurred on 20.08.2011.
Claimant aged 23 years working as mechanic and earning `10,000/-, however, tribunal considered his monthly income notionally at `6,000/-, ignoring fact that claimant was a skilled worker.
8. It was submitted that since disability assessed was substantial, addition of future prospects would be justified.
It was submitted that as per Ex.P.6 disability assessed to right lower limb was 40% and 25% in respect of left lower limb.
Considering occupation of claimant as mechanic, assessment of disability was on lower side and any scope for reduction under future prospects by 50% would be clearly off-set.
Hence, there was no merit in insurer's appeal.
Shri Babu H.Metagudda, learned counsel for respondent no.2/owner supported judgment.
It was submitted that in para 7 of memorandum of appeal, insurer admitted that driver of insured vehicle was holding driving licence to drive heavy passenger vehicle/heavy transport vehicle.

But, as per notification no.SO-436(e) dated 12.06.1989 issued by Central Government, under Section 41(4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 classified crane mounted vehicle as a non-transport vehicle and since appellant admitted that driver was having licence to drive heavy passenger vehicle and transport vehicle, same would cover class of vehicle and there was no substance in contention regarding violation of policy condition.

10. In reply, Smt.Preeti Patil Melkundi, learned counsel for appellant/insurer submitted that during cross- examination, claimant who was driver of car, other vehicle involved in accident admitted that accident in question was a head on collision and at time of accident he was not NC:
2023:KHC-K:6530 having driving licence to drive car.
Said admission per se would establish negligence against claimant.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel.
Perused impugned judgment and award and record.

12. From above submission and since only insurer is in appeal challenging finding of tribunal on contributory negligence, on quantum, on liability as well as denial of opportunity, points that would arise for consideration are :
"i) Whether tribunal committed error in not granting adequate opportunity of leading evidence to appellant ?
ii) Whether finding of tribunal on liability calls for interference ?
iii) Whether finding of tribunal on contributory negligence calls for interference ?
iv) Whether assessment of compensation by tribunal calls for modification ?"
Point no.(i) :
13.

Insofar as violation of principles of natural justice, it is seen that claim petition was filed on NC:
2023:KHC-K:6530 13.12.2011.
Upon issuance of notice, insurer filed objections on 27.12.2012.
On perusal of order-sheet, it is seen that recording of evidence of claimant was concluded on 20.01.2015.
On same day, insurer filed I.A.no.4 under Section 170 of M.V.Act.

Submits no objection,
it was allowed.
On said date, counsel for claimant submitted no further evidence and matter was adjourned to 30.01.2015 for arguments.
At request of insurer, matter was adjourned to 19.02.2015.

On said date, learned Member of Tribunal records that counsel for insurer sought time and inspite of giving sufficient time, respondent failed to lead evidence and therefore respondent evidence was taken as 'nil' and matter was posted on 26.02.2015 for arguments.
On said date, insurer filed I.A.no.5 under Section 151 of Code of Civil Procedure for reopening of evidence.
Said application came to be rejected.
On 09.03.2015, in view of failure of counsel for insurer to appear, matter was adjourned to 16.03.2015 and thereafter to 25.03.2015.
On 18.04.2015, impugned award came to be passed.
In NC: 2023:KHC-K:6530 meanwhile, it is seen that insurer had filed two other applications for reopening of evidence.
14. Though it is contended by respondents herein that counsel for insurer had submitted that it had no evidence to lead.

Order-sheet of 19.02.2015, reads as follows :-
"19-2-15 Petitioner absent.
Clmnt.
by SMR Adv.
Respondent absent.
R1 by SKR Adv.
PVM Advocate prays time.
R2 by PVM Adv.
Perused.
Sufficient time is given.
For R/1 Hence, respondents evidence is taken as no evidence.

sentences.text: For arguments.

15. Even if order dated 19.02.2015, can be read as a concession by counsel, same would not bind insurer.
Therefore, there was no justification for rejection of I.As.no.5, 6 and 7.
Tribunal ought to have allowed applications atleast on terms.
Failure to afford opportunity would go to root of matter.
Hence, point no.(i) is answered in affirmative.
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6530 16. Point no.(ii) to (iv) :
In view of finding on point no.(i) and since matter requires to be remanded back to Tribunal.

Therefore, it would be appropriate to set- side impugned award and remand matter back to tribunal permitting appellant/ insurer to lead evidence and thereafter directing tribunal to pass fresh award in accordance with law.
Points no.(ii) to (iv) are answered accordingly.
17. Contentions of both parties on said issues is kept open to be re-agitated before tribunal.

Since matter is of year 2011 and 12 years have already lapsed,
appellant/insurer is directed to lead evidence and conclude same within time frame.
Since all parties are represented they are directed to appear before Tribunal without awaiting fresh notice.

Hence, following :
ORDER Appeal is allowed in part.
Impugned award is set-aside.
Matter is remitted back to Tribunal for fresh consideration.
All parties shall appear before Tribunal on 25.09.2023.
Thereafter, insurer is granted a period of two months to lead and conclude evidence.
Tribunal shall record evidence, if necessary on day to day basis.
Respondents herein shall conclude cross-examination as early as possible.
In case of request for opportunity to lead further evidence by claimant, tribunal shall consider same granting same in time bond manner.
